notable_absence.finding: Examine is a read-only operation (it retrieves document instances, changes nothing) but is implemented as a POST with no dedicated Required Permissions section, gated to Full Admin only - the SAME restrictive pattern as the write operations (archive, create, delete), not the broader Full Admin/Backup Full Admin/Read-Only Admin pattern used by the four genuine GET list/info endpoints (backup-get-cluster-info.md, backup-get-expired-backups.md, backup-get-plan-info.md, backup-get-repository-info.md). A reader cannot tell from HTTP verb alone which permission tier an endpoint needs; examine-data is the clearest case of the mismatch, since its own description states it only 'retrieves' data.

cross_component_finding: STRONGEST SINGLE PIECE OF EVIDENCE IN THIS BATCH FOR ROUND 11's 'SAME CONSTRUCT' FINDING. This page's `data_path` field description - 'The bucket, scope, and collection within which the document resides. The names must be specified in order of containment, period-separated: for example, `travel-sample._default._default`' - is not merely analogous to cbbackupmgr's collection-string mechanism (backup:collection-string, extraction-layer from cbbackupmgr-info.json), it is IDENTICAL in shape down to the same example-style dot-separated bucket.scope.collection format. The REST API's own JSON field is simply a renamed carrier (`data_path` vs cbbackupmgr's `--collection-string` flag) for the exact same addressing convention the CLI uses to locate data inside a repository. This is independent confirmation, from a completely different endpoint family (data retrieval, not repository/plan management) than backup-create-repository.json's archive/bucket_name evidence, that the Backup Service REST API and cbbackupmgr are built on one shared internal data model, accessed through two differently-shaped but semantically identical surfaces - reinforcing rather than merely repeating round 11's finding.
